title: Patterned Wafer Inspection - Pattern Defects Detection on Teron 640
subtitle: Post-Oxidation Quality Validation for 28nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Klaus Weber

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Teron 640 system to detect and classify Pattern Defects defects during post-oxidation inspection at the 28nm technology node. The test is conducted at Hsinchu Fab 12 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 300mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Pattern Defects defects that are critical to yield at the 28nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Teron 640 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Teron 640
- Inspection Type: Patterned Wafer Inspection
- Target Defect: Pattern Defects
- Process Step: Post-Oxidation
- Wafer Size: 300mm
- Technology Node: 28nm
- Fab Location: Hsinchu Fab 12

This test case applies to all Teron 640 systems deployed at Hsinchu Fab 12 for post-oxidation monitoring in the 28nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Teron 640
Software Version: v13.3.355
Recipe: PATTERNED_WAFER_INSPECTION_28nm_POST_OXIDATION
Illumination Mode: Brightfield
Scan Speed: Medium (160 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 1.0μm
Edge Exclusion: 2mm
Sampling Plan: 5-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Teron 640 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Patterned Wafer Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Pattern Defects defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 28nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 58 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 94% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±1.0% for Patterned Wafer Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.99 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2025-04-16
Wafers Tested: 20
Total Defects Found: 2966
Defect Density: 419.6 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 4.4%
Capture Rate: 86.9%
Test Duration: 285 minutes
System Uptime: 97.1%

Result Classification: PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Teron 640 demonstrated excellent performance in detecting Pattern Defects at the 28nm node.

b) The capture rate requires optimization of the detection algorithm.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) Throughput metrics met production requirements without sensitivity compromise.

e) The system successfully integrated with the factory automation host.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS: No corrective actions required. Test passed all acceptance criteria.
